facts.fact: The report of September 2015, by the Department of Civil and National Registration with the University of Botswana and the World Bank, states that births and deaths documentation passes online from local and regional offices to a central national data repository, which is connected to outstations so that changes and updates to registrations are made in real time.

The September 2015 report states that both births and deaths are transferred online from local and regional offices to the central repository, and that electronic on-site registration in hospitals covers births and deaths.

The September 2015 report states that electronic on-site registration of births and deaths in hospitals began in 2011 and had opened in 13 hospitals; it gives the department's network as 37 stations in 12 districts and 25 sub-districts but does not say how many of the 37 are connected to the central repository.

The September 2015 report states that the Department of Civil and National Registration, a government department within the Ministry of Labour and Home Affairs with 454 staff, delivers civil registration and identity management under the Births and Deaths Registration Act and the National Registration Act.
The September 2015 report lists as its way forward a 2015-2020 CRVS and Identity Management Investment Plan; the captured excerpt gives the plan's title only, not its content.
